question: At what age should an infant start receiving other foods alongside breast milk?

options.D: At the end of the sixth month

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first six months, meaning complementary foods should only start at that point. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is allowed during exclusive breastfeeding?
explanation: Vitamins, mineral supplements, or medicines prescribed by a clinician are allowed, but no water or other liquids. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for milk production in the breast alveoli?
explanation: Prolactin drives the actual synthesis and secretion of milk within the breast tissue. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the main job of oxytocin during breastfeeding?
explanation: Oxytocin causes the muscles around the milk glands to squeeze milk forward into the ducts for the baby. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why is colostrum often called the baby's first immunization?

options.A: It acts as a strong pain reliever for newborns
options.B: It builds the bone structure of the infant
options.C: It contains high amounts of protective antibodies
options.D: It provides all the daily iron the baby needs

explanation: Colostrum is packed with immunoglobulins like IgA that line the gut and protect against invading pathogens. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h3)

question: How does hindmilk differ from foremilk during a single nursing session?

options.A: Hindmilk has a higher water content
options.C: Hindmilk contains more fat and calories
options.D: Hindmilk is produced only at night

explanation: As the feed continues, the fat content increases, providing the calorie-dense hindmilk required for satiety and weight gain. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h3)

question: Within what timeframe should breastfeeding ideally be started after birth?

options.B: Only after the placenta is delivered

explanation: Early initiation within the first hour takes advantage of the newborn's alert state and stimulates successful lactation. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h4)

question: A postpartum mother has severe nipple pain and cracked skin during feeds. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The infant has oral thrush infection

explanation: When a baby only latches onto the nipple instead of taking a large mouthful of the areola, trauma and pain occur. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h4)

question: About how many extra daily calories does a woman need while exclusively breastfeeding?
explanation: Milk production requires substantial energy, leading to an increased daily caloric requirement for the mother. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h5)

question: When should a breastfeeding mother be advised to drink fluids?
explanation: Thirst is the best natural guide for maintaining proper hydration during lactation without forcing excessive water consumption. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is a common misconception about colostrum that midwives frequently encounter?

options.A: It is produced in excessive quantities
options.B: It causes immediate infant weight gain
options.C: It cures all childhood infections instantly
options.D: It is dirty and should be discarded

explanation: A widespread myth is that the yellowish first milk is stale or harmful, whereas it is actually lifesaving and protective. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h6)

question: A mother has a hot, red, painful breast and a high fever two weeks postpartum. What is the appropriate management step?

options.A: Encourage continued milk removal and refer for antibiotics
options.B: Advise immediate cessation of breastfeeding on both sides
options.C: Prescribe strong sleeping tablets for the mother
options.D: Apply tight bandages to suppress milk production

explanation: Stopping breastfeeding worsens mastitis; milk must be removed regularly alongside medical treatment for infection. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h6)

question: How many wet diapers per day typically show that an exclusively breastfed infant is getting enough milk?
explanation: Six or more pale, wet diapers daily show that the baby is receiving adequate fluid intake from breast milk. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which finding is most reassuring regarding a two-week-old baby's nutrition status?

options.A: The birth weight has been successfully regained
options.B: The infant refuses to feed during the night
options.C: The baby sleeps continuously for ten hours
options.D: The stools are consistently hard and dry

explanation: Regaining birth weight by around two weeks of age confirms that milk transfer and intake are adequate. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why must complementary foods be introduced alongside breastfeeding at six months?

options.A: Infants naturally reject breast milk at this stage
options.B: The baby's teeth are fully grown by this age
options.C: Breast milk alone can no longer meet iron and zinc needs
options.D: Breast milk production completely stops at six months

explanation: Growing nutritional stores mean breast milk needs supplementation with iron-rich foods from six months onward. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h8)

question: When introducing new foods to an infant, what practice is recommended?

options.A: Stop breastfeeding entirely on the day foods begin
options.B: Mix multiple new foods together on the very first day
options.C: Add plenty of hot chili spices to stimulate appetite
options.D: Introduce one single food at a time to check for reactions

explanation: Testing one food at a time helps easily identify any food allergy or intolerance if it occurs. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h8)
